paragraphs: Walmart item setup errors are easier to resolve when you connect the exact error to the exact item and field. Start with the failed submission, preserve the original data, and make a correction you can verify. Repeatedly uploading a whole catalog without a diagnosis makes it harder to explain which file produced the current result.

Create a small working record before editing: submission time, file name, Feed ID if available, affected SKU, product ID, exact error text, and the field named in the report. Keep the original spreadsheet and downloaded error report unchanged. Work on a clearly named copy so another team member can trace the correction.

Separate four questions: did the file upload, did the item process, is the offer published, and did the intended content appear? Each answer determines the next check. An upload confirmation alone does not close the task.

sections.title: Find the affected SKU in Activity Feed
paragraphs: Walmart’s Activity Feed guide says a Feed ID tracks item setup and maintenance submissions. Open the relevant feed and select the number in the Errors column to see affected SKUs and messages. For several errors, download the spreadsheet through the Error report column. Walmart explicitly advises monitoring Activity Feed even after an upload-complete message.

Match that report to your saved source file before changing anything. Group repeated messages so you can investigate a shared cause, but still review each affected item. A correction that fits one product may be wrong for another product type or variation.

Walmart allows either correcting and resubmitting the original feed or creating a new feed containing only failed items. Choose the smaller, traceable correction where appropriate. Keep the successful items out of repeated troubleshooting unless their data also needs a deliberate update. Follow the labels available in your account if its layout differs from the published guide.

sections.title: Protect existing content before resubmitting
paragraphs: Walmart’s item setup FAQ warns that an updated template should include information you want to retain. Its example is images: submitting new images while omitting existing ones can leave only the new images on the listing. Treat a repair as a catalog update that deserves a before-and-after check.

Before submission, compare the working copy with your retained product record and current listing. Confirm that existing images and other intended information remain present. Keep a simple change log listing each SKU, field, previous value, replacement value, and reason. This is a practical control for your team, rather than an additional Walmart requirement.

Inspect the saved file itself after editing. Confirm that each correction stayed on the right row and that unrelated values were preserved. Avoid combining a feed repair with a broad content rewrite: a focused file is easier to review and diagnose if another error appears.

sections.title: Use the error message to choose the correction
paragraphs: For required-field, length, or allowed-value errors, follow the template’s field requirements. For missing attribute metadata, Walmart advises a fresh spreadsheet if you cannot identify what changed; preserve rows 1–6. Its setup troubleshooting guide also describes highlighted error cells. Correct those cells instead of rebuilding the template structure.

For a product ID error, check the barcode against the packaging or manufacturer information and confirm the exact quantity and version. Look for typing or copying mistakes. Walmart says never to invent an identifier; an item without one may need the documented GTIN exemption route. Do not borrow a similar product’s identifier just to clear validation.

For an image URL error, check the actual address submitted. Walmart’s image guide lists publicly inaccessible URLs, HTML pages, and URLs containing a query among unsupported formats. It lists an image-file extension among supported-format requirements. Compare against the current full guide rather than assuming a link that opens in your browser qualifies.

For variant errors, check the group and attribute fields named in the report. The Full setup variant guide requires each variation as a separate item row. Review the group together so the repair still describes the products correctly. Do not assign arbitrary group values simply to remove an error.

ITEM SETUP DECISION AID

Match the symptom before you resubmit

Open the symptom you actually see. Follow the reported error or item status; these routes are a working guide, not a diagnosis of your account.

Save a trace first

Keep the Feed ID, submission time, original file, affected SKU and product ID, plus the exact message or error report.

Fewer items does not mean fewer fields

A correction feed can contain only failed items. For each updated item, include all information intended to remain: omitted fields can overwrite existing content, including images.

Choose your observed symptom

1. Template or item validation error

Inspect: Read the highlighted cell or error description. After upload, filter Activity Feed to Item Setup and open the Error Report or affected item's Errors.

Correct: Fix the named field. Check required values, allowed choices or product ID only when the message points there. Individual errors may offer Fix Error.

Retain: Preserve template metadata and dropdown formatting. If metadata rows were altered, use a fresh template.

Verify: Track the corrected submission in Activity Feed, then inspect item status and the live listing if published.

2. Technical or system error

Inspect: Confirm that the message identifies a technical processing problem rather than invalid item data.

Correct: Follow Walmart's system-error instructions. Check whether processing recovers; escalate unresolved cases with the Feed ID and spreadsheet.

Retain: Save the original error and a record of later status checks before making another submission.

Verify: Confirm the feed's final result and affected item status. A technical retry is not proof that an item is published.

Inspect: Read the current Activity Feed and item statuses. Identify any explicit compliance review, including hazardous-material review.

Correct: Follow the indicated review or processing path. Upload acceptance alone does not establish a field error to fix.

Retain: Keep the submission time, Feed ID and review message so later checks refer to the same attempt.

Verify: Check for a completed feed result, then check whether the item is published. Use the expectations for that specific status.

Inspect: Find the item in the Unpublished Items dashboard or Item Report and read its stated reason.

Correct: Follow the remediation for that reason. A processed feed and a published offer are separate checks.

Retain: Keep the reason, affected item identifiers and any requested evidence with the feed record.

Verify: Recheck publication status and the customer-facing page after the issue is resolved.

5. Item is live; your content edit is absent

Inspect: Compare the submitted value, feed result and live page. Walmart's unified catalog selects which submitted content appears.

Correct: Check the content-error guidance. If applicable, use the documented Request Content Ownership path with authorization evidence.

Retain: Save the submitted content and supporting brand or reseller authorization for the request.

Verify: Check the request outcome and live content. Feed processing alone does not prove your contribution was selected.

Record the correction, new Feed ID and final item state. Compare retained fields and images with the original record before calling the update complete.

Keep a dated record of price changes, competing promotions, exclusions, and returns so results have context.
